migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Ecosystem findings/citations were centrally re-adjudicated under the current runner-owned fixed rubric. Legacy language-local scores were not copied.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.candidate_universe: For a single-language external-ecosystem shard, the predeclared target is the language's own canonical identity: search for (a) the official/canonical repository and site declared by the language's own docs, and (b) the presence of independent third-party public-knowledge venues (Stack Overflow tag/questions, Reddit community, Discord/community chat, third-party tutorials/blog posts, books, conference talks) using a fixed query set applied identically in spirit to every other assigned language shard: '<language> programming language', '<language> stackoverflow OR reddit OR discord OR tutorial OR blog', '<language> site:stackoverflow.com OR site:reddit.com', and a GitHub popularity-signal query. Candidate universe = general web search results returned by these queries; no cherry-picking beyond the queries actually run.

component_findings.current_knowledge: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-external--part-3--quidra): Normalized 0-100 (100 = best/richest independent community knowledge). Score of 5 reflects: (a) credit for genuine, substantial first-party documentation and an official interactive playground, which lower-bounds the score above zero and above a purely non-existent/undocumented language; (b) an essentially complete absence, within the retrievable public web, of independent third-party community knowledge channels (Q&A sites, forums, chat communities, tutorials, blogs, books) that the metric is specifically measuring, which is the dominant factor and keeps the score near the low end of the scale rather than at a mid-range value reserved for languages with some but limited community presence.

metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.limitations: Web search snapshots are not exhaustive and could miss small/private community venues (e.g. a closed Discord invite-only server) that do not surface in general search indexes. | Raw popularity indicators such as GitHub star/fork counts were not retrievable via the search tool in this session (no aggregator page reported a numeric count), so this evidence relies on presence/absence signals from search results rather than a numeric popularity proxy; per methodology this is used only as declared, non-standalone evidence. | This is a single-language shard; no cross-language comparison table was computed here, only the Quidra-specific raw evidence, consistent with the language-sharded task assignment.
metric.community_public_knowledge_availa.selection_rule: Inspect the same knowledge channels for every language and use current, publicly accessible evidence rather than raw search-result counts alone.

snapshot_recertification.policy: legacy evidence re-adjudicated under current runner-owned rubric
